tasks.short: Research economic issues and disseminate findings in reports or journal articles

steps.what: Define the economic research question and study approach
Collect and verify economic data and source documentation
Specify variables, transformations and analysis parameters
Calculate the specified economic estimates and research tables
Interpret economic findings and record conclusions and limitations
Write the technical report or scientific article

loop.purpose: Draft research prose from the economist's results and conclusions
loop.input: Verified tables, interpretation notes, methods and real source references
loop.output: Report draft with linked claims and citations
loop.check: Economist checks numbers, identification claims, causal wording and limitations against the actual analysis and sources
loop.stop: One correction then manual writing for unsupported or materially changed claims
loop.why_not_simpler: A section template cannot express the specific economic argument

steps.what: Check and finish the research report or article
Disseminate the final report or submit the scientific article

tasks.design: Use native analytical routines in {DATA_PLATFORM} or {SPREADSHEET} for repeated calculations after the economist specifies the analysis. A bounded {DOCS} drafting loop uses verified results and interpretation notes; final checking and actual dissemination remain separate human steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated calculations and report prose add work after research choices are made.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable native routines and source-bound drafting can support those fragments.
tasks.still_hard: Identification, data revisions and causal interpretation require economic judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The economist judges what the data can establish and explains uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat computation and prose, with unchanged research responsibility.

reach.task: Maintain traceable economic data and definitions

evidence.claim: Native analytical routines and bounded prose drafting can support repeat economic research calculations and reports; this workflow and estimate are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes research design, data collection and checking, analysis specification, calculations, interpretation, report writing and dissemination. No research phase is supplied as free clerical input.

The economist captures source, release version, variable, period, unit and missingness in s2, then transformation, estimator, exclusions and parameter values in s3. Their full capture and checking time remains counted.

s4 native routines produce results from that checked dataset and specification; missing definitions or unsupported analyses return to manual calculation. s5 produces the actual conclusion and limitation notes used by the model.

Test native statistical routines and report templates first. Only currently repeated manual calculations gain in s4; already scripted runtime and same-system saves earn no saving. Publication acceptance is outside the economist's control, and no acceptance is assumed.
research_questions: Do reusable native routines reproduce independently checked estimates without extra preparation?
Does corrected drafting preserve every identification limit?

already_counted.description: Data and parameter capture, interpretation, draft correction and final checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain reproducible routines and source-bound drafting checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final report or article, tables, references, attachments and intended external destination checked before s8 dissemination; changes void the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R79, gross21 minus6 upkeep gives net15. Range3-8 assumes only some calculation and prose remains repetitive; design, data checking and interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop economic guidelines, standards and policy viewpoints

steps.what: Review evidence and existing economic guidelines and standards
Compare economic assumptions and implications for forecasts and policy
Develop the economic position and choose guideline recommendations
Write guidelines, standards and the economic point-of-view document

loop.purpose: Express selected economic recommendations in guidance text
loop.input: Economist's viewpoint brief and referenced evidence
loop.output: Draft guidance with conditions and references
loop.check: Economist checks the position, normative choices, conditions and uncertainty against the brief
loop.stop: One correction then manual writing if the draft changes a substantive position
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot express the selected economic position

steps.what: Check and finish the economic guidelines and viewpoint

tasks.design: Keep evidence assessment, comparisons and the economic position with the economist in {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts the chosen guidance, which the economist checks and finishes; this design does not adopt policy or send the guidance externally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing guidance repeats decisions already captured in the viewpoint brief.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can express the brief while retaining references and conditions.
tasks.still_hard: Economic standards involve normative choices and uncertain effects.
tasks.human_edge: The economist distinguishes evidence from value judgements and owns the position.
tasks.altitude: Less rewriting of a selected position; decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify how policy assumptions affect an economic standard

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting can express an economist's own guideline brief; the economic position and labour estimate remain unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual evidence reading, comparison notes, viewpoint development and the written guidance. No policy adoption or external communication is hidden in an internal document save.
The economist produces selected recommendation, rationale, source, condition and limitation in s2 and s3 at full time. No free structured policy position or agreement flag is assumed.
Existing forecast assumptions are checked as part of s2. Missing evidence or an unresolved policy choice returns to manual reasoning and writing.
Test native reusable guidance sections and tracked changes first; use a loop only for project-specific prose. Internal saves earn no saving or self-approval.
unknowns: How much guidance prose is genuinely repetitive
research_questions: Does corrected drafting preserve the exact boundary between evidence and normative recommendations?

already_counted.description: Comparison notes, viewpoint capture, draft correction and final checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and verify source references after revisions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R90, gross10 minus3 upkeep gives net7. Range1-4 assumes the position is already explicit in the brief; all substantive economic choices retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach economic theories, principles and methods

steps.what: Identify the learners' needs and select economic teaching sources
Plan the sequence of economic principles, methods and worked examples
Write teaching explanations and worked-example notes

loop.purpose: Draft teaching explanations from selected economic sources
loop.input: Lesson outline, sources and teacher-selected worked examples
loop.output: Editable explanations tied to the examples
loop.check: Economist verifies assumptions, equations, example reasoning and suitability for learner level
loop.stop: One correction then manual explanation if reasoning or arithmetic is wrong
loop.why_not_simpler: A reusable outline cannot explain the particular economic concept

steps.what: Check and finish the economics teaching materials
Teach economic theories and methods and respond to learners' questions

tasks.design: Use reusable lesson structures in {DOCS} and a bounded drafting loop for selected explanations. The economist verifies economic reasoning and examples, then teaches and responds live.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing explanations and arranging recurrent lesson structures take time beyond the teaching decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native structure reuse and checked drafting can assist preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Economic assumptions and counterintuitive results require responsive explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The economist detects misunderstanding and changes examples during teaching.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated preparation; live teaching and responsibility stay human.

reach.task: Explain an economic method used in a research project

evidence.claim: Native outline reuse and checked model drafting can assist economics teaching preparation; no live-teaching labour gain is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary includes content selection, lesson planning, actual written explanations, checking and live teaching. No preparation record is hidden in the conversation.
The economist produces learning aim, concept sequence, source reference and selected example in s1 and s2; capture is counted. The model receives those inputs, not a free prewritten lesson.
Missing sources or incorrect reasoning returns to manual writing. Worked-example values and arithmetic are checked by the economist; no synthetic learner assessment is used.
Test native reusable lesson structures first. The gain in s2 is repeated structure only; internal document saves have no saving or self-gate.
research_questions: Does checked drafting save preparation after every worked example is independently verified?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and final teaching-material checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain reusable lesson structures and source-bound drafting examples.

approvals.approved_version: Exact prepared teaching-material version and intended learner group checked in s4; changed prepared explanations require a new check before s5 delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R89, gross11 minus3 upkeep gives net8. Range1-4 assumes reused structures and corrected prose help; live teaching and questions retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Testify at policy hearings and present cost-benefit recommendations

steps.what: Review policy changes and the supporting cost-benefit analyses
Develop recommendations and record the intended testimony argument
Write the prepared hearing statement and recommendation explanations

loop.purpose: Draft the economist's intended prepared statement
loop.input: Argument notes and verified cost-benefit evidence
loop.output: Statement draft linked to the evidence
loop.check: Economist checks effects, assumptions, uncertainty and recommendation wording against the actual analysis and intended position
loop.stop: One correction then manual statement writing if implications are changed or unsupported
loop.why_not_simpler: A statement template cannot express the specific economic argument

steps.what: Check and finalize the hearing statement and supporting exhibits
Submit the final written statement and exhibits to the hearing organiser
Testify at the hearing and present recommendations while answering questions

tasks.design: Use a bounded {DOCS} drafting aid for the economist's prepared statement from verified cost-benefit evidence and argument notes. The economist checks the final version, submits it through {EMAIL}, then personally testifies and answers questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing the prepared statement repeats an argument already developed from the evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can assist the wording while retaining evidence links.
tasks.still_hard: The economist must defend assumptions and respond to unexpected policy questions.
tasks.human_edge: The economist explains uncertainty and remains accountable for the testimony.
tasks.altitude: A small preparation gain; testimony and policy recommendations stay human.

reach.task: Explain uncertain policy costs and benefits at a hearing

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting can express an economist's own hearing argument from supplied analyses; no legal or economic judgement is delegated, and the time estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes evidence review, recommendation and argument notes, actual statement writing, checking, written submission and live testimony. Original cost-benefit analysis is produced by its research workflow, not assumed to be a free finished statement.
The economist checks analysis source, version, assumptions and results in s1 and captures recommendation, rationale, effect estimate and uncertainty in s2. Their full time remains counted.
Missing evidence or an unresolved position returns to manual preparation; no structured recommendation or hearing-ready argument is assumed.

Test native statement templates and reference reuse first. The loop assists wording only. Internal saves have no saving or self-gate; the actual submission and prepared oral version have explicit final-version checks.
unknowns: Whether a written submission is required
research_questions: Does corrected drafting preserve the conditions on every cost-benefit claim?

already_counted.description: Argument capture, draft correction, final evidence checks and submission checks remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain source-bound statement instructions and check drafting failures.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final statement, exhibits and hearing-organiser recipient checked before s5 submission; changes void the check.
Exact prepared testimony version, evidence and intended hearing checked in s4; changed prepared content requires recheck before s6, while live answers remain the economist's judgement.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R94, gross6 minus2 upkeep gives net4. Range0-2 assumes a written prepared statement benefits from checked wording; recommendations, evidence checking and live testimony retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Economic reasoning, research design and public explanation stay with the economist; selected repeated calculations and prose become shorter.
reach: Work with research assistants on traceable datasets
Compare policy assumptions with environmental economists
skills_to_grow: Check source-bound prose against actual estimates
Preserve uncertainty in teaching and testimony
role.ambitious_version: An economist with more time for defensible reasoning and evidence checking and less repeated computation and document preparation.
